text.p: With world record-holders Dan O'Brien and Jackie Joyner-Kersee not competing, Chris Huffins and Kym Carter dominated the multi-events Wednesday on a low-key opening day to the U.S. athletics championships.
Huffins, 10th in the Atlanta Olympics decathlon, led two of the five events and accumulated 4,499 points before hometown fans for a 165-point advantage over fourth-place Atlanta finisher Steve Fritz.
Carter, a 1992 Olympian, scored well in the high jump and shot put to pace the heptathlon with 3,854 points. She was 37 points ahead of DeDee Nathan.
No finals were decided as the championships began a five-day run to determine the American team for Athens world championships in August.
O'Brien, the decathlon world record-holder, is out of the meeting because of a stress fracture. Heptathlon record-holder Joyner-Kersee is competing only in the women's long jump.
"I thought I put up some pretty solid marks," said Huffins, who won the 100 meters in 10.35 seconds and topped performances in the long jump with a leap of 7.79 meters.
"I'd like to score between 4,000 and 4,100 points tomorrow. I may not win, but it will definitely get me on the team," he said.
Carter won the shot with a put of 15.46 meters and shared the high jump lead at 1.80 meters.
Olympian C.J. Hunter led qualifying in the men's shot with a best of 20.73 meters.
U.S. record-holder Johnny Gray paced men's 800-meter qualifying in one minute, 47.68 seconds.
